money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is Mozambique Metical (MZN). It's illegal to export or import MZN. You can get MZN by exchanging: traveller's cheques, in US dollars or Euros, at major banks in Maputo You can only change traveller's cheques for MZN. It's difficult to change traveller's cheques outside of Maputo. You may be charged a high rate of commission. In Maputo, ATMs will often accept international credit cards. laws.rule: National Conservation Law 16/2014, as amended and republished by Law 5/2017: article 16 restricts hunting, resource extraction, habitat/landform alteration, water pollution, disturbance to flora/fauna/ecological processes or cultural heritage, and introducing species in national parks, subject to stated scientific/management exceptions. Human presence is under controlled management-plan conditions, not unrestricted access. This national rule is held once, not copied as provincial law.

Article 41 of the 2017 republication: activities in conservation areas must comply with the law, regulations and management plan; compatible uses may need direct area-administration authorisation. This does not mean every ordinary visit requires a separate research permit, nor that a park ticket allows every activity. Site-specific permissions and any later amendments are not yet comprehensively checked.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: A visa is needed. Mozambique's National Migration Service runs an eVisa and eTA portal (launched 11 February 2026). Australia isn't on the visa-exempt or 30-day eTA lists, so Australians apply for the eVisa: tourist or business, for 90 days or less.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist or business eVisa online: apply, pay, then print the preliminary eVisa for boarding and arrival.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Apply on evisa.gov.mz, pay, and print the approved eVisa. Bring long-form birth certificates (and translated notarised consent) for children. Carry a yellow fever certificate if arriving from a yellow fever country.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Tourist and business eVisas cover stays of 90 days or less.

steps.step: Apply on the official eVisa portal with the passport you'll travel on, upload the documents and pay.
Download and print the preliminary eVisa from the email; show it at boarding and on arrival.
Carry a yellow fever certificate if arriving from a yellow fever country: without it you can be detained and returned.
With children under 18, carry long-form birth certificates and, if a parent is absent, a notarised consent translated into Portuguese.

documents: Yellow fever certificate if arriving from a yellow fever country
Children: long-form birth certificate, translated notarised parental consent if needed
